label: Graphing Linear Equations
overview: A linear equation in two variables produces a straight line on the coordinate plane. SAT questions ask you to read slope and intercepts from a graph or equation, identify the correct graph for a given equation, or find where a line crosses an axis. Mastering slope-intercept form y = mx + b is the foundation.

conceptDiagram.caption: y = mx + b: slope m controls steepness, b is where the line crosses the y-axis

workedExamples.problem: The line 4x + 2y = 12 is graphed in the xy-plane. What are its slope and y-intercept?

steps.title: Convert to slope-intercept form
steps.content: Isolate y by subtracting 4x and dividing by 2.

steps.title: Read off m and b
steps.content: The coefficient of x is the slope; the constant is the y-intercept.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading the x-intercept as the y-intercept from a graph
commonMistakes.fix: The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis (x = 0). The x-intercept is where it crosses the x-axis (y = 0).

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting the slope sign wrong when the line goes downward
commonMistakes.fix: A line going from upper-left to lower-right has a negative slope (rise is negative when run is positive).

quickTip: To graph quickly from y = mx + b: plot the y-intercept (0, b), then move rise/run from that point to get a second point, and connect.
